title: Session permissions for Forge Git queries
summary: The change-request panel runs its Git queries under the session's own sandbox mode and subprocess provider instead of forcing read-only confinement. Command-local Git configuration disables clean and process filters, alongside the existing hook and external-diff restrictions, so inspection never runs code configured by the repository.
firstReason: The session is the authority for filesystem permission, and background inspection must not execute repository-configured helpers. Both are security rules for any host that runs Git.

title: Forge changes view responsiveness
summary: The changes view of a large change request (366 files in the measured case) stays responsive: CSS `:has()` rules are scoped to navigator rows, memoized file sections receive stable values, and an expanded file draws its lines only when it comes near the viewport.
firstReason: The requirement (a very large diff must not freeze the page or slow the rest of the application) stands, and the scoped-CSS finding applies to any HTML. The React memoization does not; the Go UI gets the same effect by rendering file sections on the host and loading them as they come into view.

title: Explicit worktree creation
summary: An experimental tool, `enter_worktree`, creates a named branch and checkout from a pinned local commit under `.agents/worktrees` and moves the session into it through the working-directory service. Creation never fetches, never copies uncommitted files and never widens the session's sandbox policy.
firstReason: An isolated checkout per session is needed for parallel agent work, and running Git through the session's own subprocess and sandbox providers keeps one permission model.

title: Change request panel and worktree Sessions
summary: An experimental two-part feature shows a session's change requests with checks, reviews and mergeability, and offers sessions that work in their own worktree. The host half assembles everything the panel shows into one streamed state, and one default-disabled Plugins entry enables the whole code-change workflow.
firstReason: A host half that assembles one streamed state per session is already the shape a server-rendered panel fed by server-sent events needs. The React half is expressed again as templates under DH-ADR-3.

title: Session change request bindings
summary: Change requests are bound to a session by a projection over its log: it reads `gh pr create`, `gh pr view` and `git push` calls and their results, so no separate store exists and bindings survive fork and resume. A provider-neutral registry shares polling, and the GitHub provider reads through the GitHub CLI on the host, so credentials never enter the session's execution environment.
firstReason: Deriving bindings from the log keeps one source of truth, and leaving forge credentials in the vendor tool's own store is a security choice. Both are language-neutral.

title: Forge state in the Session list
summary: Each session-list row shows a branch glyph while the session works in its own worktree, and the glyph of its most urgent change request, with a hover card naming the branch and up to three change requests. The facts reach the list as cached projection views, so sessions that are not loaded show them too.
firstReason: It is a display rule fed by host projections, which a server-rendered list can read directly; DH-ADR-3 changes only the rendering.

title: Pull request comment drafts in the code host's pending review
summary: A pull request comment the user keeps for later is stored in the user's pending review on the code host, not in the browser. The changes view shows pending comments with the host's threads, and every write re-checks the head commit and is never retried.
firstReason: Keeping drafts on the code host removes a second store and makes drafts started elsewhere visible. It also suits a server-rendered UI, which has no browser-side store; the small remainder upstream keeps in the browser (review summary, publication records) needs a host-side home that the forge area must choose.

title: Forge provider command rules
summary: Each code-host provider registers a declarative rule that describes its command-line tool (`gh`, `glab`): which subcommands create or reference a change request and how to map a parsed command to a URL. The shared package keeps the tokenizer and the projection, and the projection's version is derived from the set of registered rules so that a checkpoint built under other rules is discarded.
firstReason: Declarative, pure rules keep recognition deterministic for replay and let a new code host be added without editing the shared package. Both properties are wanted in Go, where each provider is a compiled-in component that registers its rule.

title: Code review page
summary: A Code review page lists the open change requests that ask for the user's review, that the user created, or that involve the user, and shows one of them in full without needing a session. The lists are read only while the page is open, and only the shown change request is polled.
firstReason: The feature and its host-side rules (optional provider capability, one search per list, reads by URL limited to callers allowed to use the host's code-host credentials) stand. The page itself is rendered by the Go host instead of being a React page.
